title: Zosia Mamet says Mad Men creator made set 'absolutely horrible'
summary: Despite its storied run, Mad Men had an 'absolutely horrible' on-set vibe, says actor Zosia Mamet, which pushed her to drop out of a recurring role.

image.caption: Actor Zosia Mamet, seen in New York in 2025, revealed on a podcast this week that the set of AMC's prestige drama Mad Men was 'absolutely horrible' due to showrunner Matthew Weiner. (Evan Agostini/Invision/AP)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Despite its storied run, Mad Men had an 'absolutely horrible' on-set vibe, says actor Zosia Mamet, which pushed her to drop out of a recurring role.
'That bro rules with fear,' actor said on Dax Shepard's Armchair Expert podcast

Mad Men earned many accolades during its nearly decade-long run, but actor Zosia Mamet has revealed that an "absolutely horrible" and "sour" vibe on set pushed her to withdraw from a recurring role on the prestige drama.

Though she found the cast of the 1960s-era ad agency series wonderful, her experience was "so terrible" due to creator and showrunner Matthew Weiner, Mamet revealed in an episode of Dax Shepard's podcast Armchair Expert, which appeared on Monday.
"That bro rules with fear," she said.
Mamet recalled, for instance, Weiner threatening the cast at every rehearsal if they dared take scripts home.
"He would be like, 'If I see that, I'm going to find you and I'm going to hunt you down. I'm going to kill you. Like, just kidding. Actually not,'" she told podcast hosts Shepard and Monica Padman.
"What are the things in Harry Potter that, when they show up, it gets cold?... When he would show up on-set, it was like a Dementor had landed."
Mamet portrayed Joyce Ramsay, a junior magazine photo editor who befriends Peggy Olson (Elisabeth Moss, one of Mad Men's leads), in a handful of episodes across seasons 4 and 5.

Writing about abusive bosses in her 2025 book of essays, Mamet recalled an intense dressing down by an unnamed TV showrunner upset with how she held an envelope during the rehearsal of a particular scene.

items: Zosia Mamet was in a Nyquil-induced haze when she auditioned for Girls

blocks.text: She revealed in the podcast that it was Weiner and described why, though she'd been in talks to extend her run on Mad Men, she couldn't stick around.
"He just like systematically dressed me down for like 45 minutes and I was like, 'I want to kill myself,'" Mamet recalled.
Just 19 or 20 years old at the time, "my level of insecurity was so great that I knew I wouldn't be able to perform... And the fear of that happening again was just too great."

Mad Men cast and crew, including from left, Elisabeth Moss, Jon Hamm, Matthew Weiner and Christina Hendricks, gather in the press room at the Primetime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles in 2011. (Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images)

Created by Weiner, a former writer and executive producer of The Sopranos, Mad Men was a cultural phenomenon that won a raft of awards across its run, including four consecutive best drama series wins at the Emmy Awards for its first four seasons. The series ended in 2015.
Two years later, while touring to promote his debut novel, Weiner was accused of sexual harassment by a former Mad Men writer and supported by a veteran producer on the show.
Weiner, who rejected the allegation as untrue, acknowledged being "demanding" and "angry a lot of the time" during Mad Men.

"Especially in the early years, it was very hard to do it. I had a lot of stress," he said at a Los Angeles book event in late 2017. "So I guess if I could do it over again, I would do it differently."
Girls co-stars, from left, Allison Williams, Zosia Mamet, Jemima Kirke and Lena Dunham appear at the New York premiere of the HBO series in 2013. (Evan Agostini/Invision/Associated Press)

Beyond her experience on Mad Men, Mamet touched on a multitude of other topics during the wide-ranging Armchair Expert interview, including her anxiety and rocky teen years, hailing from a famous theatre-world family, and acting in films and shows like Parenthood and Girls.
The latter is set for a short revival that's set to start filming in 2027.
